Barbell Back Squat — 3RM strength test ramp
Barbell Bench Press — 3RM strength test ramp
Goblet Squat (substitute for barbell back squat)
Safety Bar Squat (substitute for barbell back squat)
Trap Bar Deadlift (substitute for conventional deadlift)
Smith Machine Squat (substitute for barbell back squat)

notes: Begin each Upper A session with 8–10 minutes of general warm-up (rowing, cycling, or brisk walking) followed by dynamic upper-body mobility: arm circles, band pull-aparts, thoracic rotations, and two warm-up sets on the first compound movement at 40% and 60% of working weight.
Lower A warm-up: 5 minutes light cardio, then hip 90/90 stretches, bodyweight squats, and goblet squat with a 5-second pause at the bottom, plus two warm-up sets on the squat.
Upper B warm-up: Band pull-aparts, face pulls with band, scapular retractions, and two warm-up sets on the first compound movement.
Lower B warm-up: Glute bridges, banded clamshells, hip flexor stretch, and two warm-up sets on the deadlift.
Phase 2 Upper A warm-up includes two additional warm-up sets on the bench press at 50% and 70% of working weight.
Week 3: Introduce a 2-second pause at the bottom of the squat and at the chest on the bench press to increase time under tension.
Week 7: Use cluster sets on the deadlift — 4 × (2+2) with a 20-second intra-set rest — to allow heavier loading while maintaining technical quality.
Week 12 deload (Monday–Thursday): Reduce all working sets to 3 sets, drop load to approximately 60–65% of Phase 3 working weights, RPE capped at 5–6; sessions should feel almost easy.
Week 12 optional testing day (Friday or Saturday): Work up to a 3RM on back squat, conventional deadlift, and bench press using a prescribed ramp protocol; rest 4–5 minutes between heavy attempts.
If three or more daily readiness scores (sleep quality, muscle soreness, motivation, general energy) are below 5 out of 10, reduce that session's intensity by 20% and do not attempt personal records.
Active recovery on Wednesday and non-training weekend day: 20–30 minutes of low-intensity activity (walking, light cycling, yoga, or swimming).
Foam rolling or targeted massage for 10 minutes post-session on quads, hamstrings, glutes, and thoracic spine is recommended.
Do not increase accessory load in Phase 3; goal is to preserve hypertrophy stimulus without adding systemic fatigue.
If any movement causes pain (not discomfort), substitute immediately.
Record every working set — weight, reps, and RPE — and review the log weekly.

# 12-Week Strength & Hypertrophy Programme

**Client Profile:** Female, 26 | Recreational lifter | Combined OCP user | Full intensity clearance
**Programme Start:** 1 June 2026
**Primary Goals:** Strength development + body composition improvement
**Training Frequency:** 4 sessions per week
**Session Duration:** 60–75 minutes

---

## Programme Overview & Periodisation Logic

The programme is divided into three four-week phases, each building on the last through progressive overload, increasing intensity, and strategic deload. The structure follows a **linear-to-undulating periodisation model**: Phase 1 establishes movement quality and a hypertrophic base; Phase 2 introduces heavier loading and strength-specific rep ranges; Phase 3 peaks intensity, consolidates strength gains, and includes a structured deload in Week 12.

Training is split across four sessions per week using an **Upper/Lower format**, which allows adequate frequency per muscle group (twice weekly), manageable session volume, and sufficient recovery between sessions. Sessions are labelled A and B within each day type, alternating stimulus between push-dominant and pull-dominant patterns.

**Weekly Template:**

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Monday | Upper A |
| Tuesday | Lower A |
| Thursday | Upper B |
| Friday/Saturday | Lower B |
| Wednesday, Sunday | Rest or active recovery |

---

## Phase 1 — Foundation & Hypertrophic Base (Weeks 1–4)

**Phase Goals:** Establish movement patterns under load, build connective tissue tolerance, accumulate volume in the 8–12 rep hypertrophy range, and develop a baseline of work capacity. Loads should feel challenging but technically clean — aim for RPE 6–7 across most working sets, leaving 3–4 reps in reserve.

**Phase 1 Intensity Guidelines:** 65–72% of estimated 1RM on compound lifts. Accessory work is load-secondary — technique and muscle connection take priority.

---

### Week 1

**Upper A — Push Focus**

Begin each session with 8–10 minutes of general warm-up (rowing, cycling, or brisk walking) followed by dynamic upper-body mobility: arm circles, band pull-aparts, thoracic rotations, and two warm-up sets on the first compound movement at 40% and 60% of working weight.

- Barbell Bench Press — 3 × 10 @ RPE 6. Focus on controlled eccentric (3 seconds down), full chest stretch at the bottom, and a strong drive through the mid-foot contact point of the bench. Rest 90 seconds.
- Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press — 3 × 12 @ RPE 6. Neutral grip acceptable if shoulder mobility is limited. Rest 90 seconds.
- Cable Chest Fly — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Emphasise the stretch and squeeze; this is a pure hypertrophy movement. Rest 60 seconds.
- Tricep Rope Pushdown — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Rest 60 seconds.
- Lateral Raise (Dumbbell) — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Slight forward lean, lead with the elbow. Rest 60 seconds.
- Dead Bug — 3 × 8 per side. Core stability finisher; slow and deliberate. Rest 45 seconds.

**Lower A — Squat Focus**

Warm-up: 5 minutes light cardio, then hip 90/90 stretches, bodyweight squats, and goblet squat with a 5-second pause at the bottom. Two warm-up sets on the squat.

- Barbell Back Squat — 3 × 10 @ RPE 6. Prioritise depth and bracing. If back squat is uncomfortable, substitute goblet squat or safety bar squat this week and progress to barbell next week. Rest 2 minutes.
- Romanian Deadlift (RDL) — 3 × 12 @ RPE 6. Hinge from the hip, soft knee, bar stays close to the legs. This is a hamstring and glute primer. Rest 90 seconds.
- Leg Press — 3 × 12 @ RPE 6. Moderate foot placement, full range of motion. Rest 90 seconds.
- Walking Lunge — 3 × 10 per leg @ bodyweight or light dumbbells. Rest 60 seconds.
- Seated Leg Curl — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Rest 60 seconds.
- Standing Calf Raise — 3 × 20. Rest 45 seconds.

**Upper B — Pull Focus**

Warm-up: Band pull-aparts, face pulls with band, scapular retractions, and two warm-up sets on the first compound movement.

- Barbell Bent-Over Row — 3 × 10 @ RPE 6. Overhand grip, hinge to roughly 45 degrees, pull to the lower sternum. Rest 90 seconds.
- Lat Pulldown — 3 × 12 @ RPE 6. Full stretch at the top, drive elbows down and back. Rest 90 seconds.
- Seated Cable Row — 3 × 12 @ RPE 6. Neutral grip, avoid excessive trunk swing. Rest 90 seconds.
- Dumbbell Bicep Curl — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Rest 60 seconds.
- Face Pull (Cable or Band) — 3 × 15. External rotation emphasis; excellent for shoulder health. Rest 60 seconds.
- Pallof Press — 3 × 10 per side. Anti-rotation core work. Rest 45 seconds.

**Lower B — Hip Hinge Focus**

Warm-up: Glute bridges, banded clamshells, hip flexor stretch, and two warm-up sets on the deadlift.

- Conventional Deadlift — 3 × 8 @ RPE 6. Establish the setup ritual: hip-width stance, bar over mid-foot, hinge to the bar, big breath and brace, drive the floor away. Rest 2 minutes.
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 3 × 10 per leg @ bodyweight or light dumbbells. This will be challenging; keep the load conservative and focus on balance and depth. Rest 90 seconds per leg.
- Hip Thrust (Barbell or Dumbbell) — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Full hip extension at the top, posterior pelvic tilt. Rest 90 seconds.
- Leg Extension — 3 × 15 @ RPE 6. Rest 60 seconds.
- Nordic Hamstring Curl or Lying Leg Curl — 3 × 10. Rest 60 seconds.
- Plank — 3 × 30 seconds. Rest 30 seconds.

---

### Weeks 2–4 — Progressive Overload Within Phase 1

The session structure and exercise selection remain identical across Weeks 2–4. Apply the following progression:

**Week 2:** Add one working set to all compound movements (now 4 sets). Increase load by 2.5–5 kg on lower body compounds and 1.25–2.5 kg on upper body compounds where RPE allows. Target RPE 6–7.

**Week 3:** Maintain 4 sets on compounds. Increase load again by the same increments. Introduce a 2-second pause at the bottom of the squat and at the chest on the bench press to increase time under tension and reinforce positional strength. Target RPE 7.

**Week 4 — Deload/Consolidation:** Reduce volume by approximately 40%. Drop back to 3 sets on all movements. Reduce load to Week 1 levels. Focus entirely on movement quality, breathing, and bracing. This is not a rest week — it is an active recovery week that allows connective tissue and the nervous system to consolidate adaptations before Phase 2 loading increases. RPE should not exceed 6.

---

## Phase 2 — Strength Development (Weeks 5–8)

**Phase Goals:** Shift the primary stimulus toward strength. Rep ranges drop on compound movements, loads increase substantially, and rest periods lengthen to allow full neuromuscular recovery between heavy sets. Accessory work remains in the hypertrophy range to continue body composition progress. Target RPE 7–8 on compound lifts.

**Phase 2 Intensity Guidelines:** 75–82% of estimated 1RM on primary compound lifts. Accessory work remains at 65–70%.

**Key Changes from Phase 1:**
- Primary compound movements shift to 4–5 sets of 4–6 reps
- Rest periods on compound movements extend to 2.5–3 minutes
- A second compound movement per session is added in the 6–8 rep range as a strength-hypertrophy bridge
- Accessory volume is maintained but not increased, to manage total fatigue

---

### Week 5

**Upper A — Push Focus**

Warm-up as Phase 1, plus two additional warm-up sets on the bench press (50%, 70% of working weight).

- Barbell Bench Press — 4 × 5 @ RPE 7–8. This is the primary strength movement of the session. Load selection is critical: the fifth rep of each set should feel genuinely hard but technically sound. Rest 3 minutes.
- Incline Dumbbell Press — 3 × 8 @ RPE 7. Strength-hypertrophy bridge. Rest 2 minutes.
- Cable Chest Fly — 3 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Overhead Tricep Extension (EZ Bar or Dumbbell) — 3 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Lateral Raise — 3 × 15. Rest 60 seconds.
- Dead Bug — 3 × 8 per side. Rest 45 seconds.

**Lower A — Squat Focus**

- Barbell Back Squat — 4 × 5 @ RPE 7–8. Rest 3 minutes.
- Front Squat or Pause Squat — 3 × 6 @ RPE 7. The front squat builds quad strength and upper back rigidity; the pause squat reinforces positional strength at the bottom. Choose based on client preference and mobility. Rest 2 minutes.
- Leg Press — 3 × 10 @ RPE 7. Rest 90 seconds.
- Walking Lunge — 3 × 10 per leg with moderate dumbbells. Rest 75 seconds.
- Seated Leg Curl — 3 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Standing Calf Raise — 3 × 20. Rest 45 seconds.

**Upper B — Pull Focus**

- Barbell Bent-Over Row — 4 × 5 @ RPE 7–8. Rest 3 minutes.
- Weighted Pull-Up or Assisted Pull-Up — 3 × 6–8. If bodyweight pull-ups are not yet achievable, use a band or lat pulldown as a substitute, but push the load hard. Rest 2 minutes.
- Seated Cable Row — 3 × 10 @ RPE 7. Rest 90 seconds.
- Dumbbell Hammer Curl — 3 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Face Pull — 3 × 15. Rest 60 seconds.
- Pallof Press — 3 × 10 per side. Rest 45 seconds.

**Lower B — Hip Hinge Focus**

- Conventional Deadlift — 4 × 4 @ RPE 7–8. Note the rep count drops to 4 here; deadlift fatigue accumulates quickly and technical breakdown at high loads is a significant injury risk. Rest 3 minutes.
- Romanian Deadlift — 3 × 8 @ RPE 7. Rest 2 minutes.
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 3 × 8 per leg with moderate dumbbells. Rest 90 seconds per leg.
- Hip Thrust — 3 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 90 seconds.
- Leg Extension — 3 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Plank — 3 × 40 seconds. Rest 30 seconds.

---

### Weeks 6–8 — Progressive Overload Within Phase 2

**Week 6:** Increase load on all compound movements by 2.5–5 kg where RPE allows. Maintain rep counts. Add one set to the primary compound in Upper A and Lower A (now 5 sets of 5). Target RPE 7–8.

**Week 7:** Increase load again. Introduce a technique called **cluster sets** on the deadlift: instead of 4 × 4, perform 4 × (2+2) with a 20-second intra-set rest. This allows heavier loading than straight sets while maintaining technical quality. Target RPE 8 on primary compounds.

**Week 8 — Deload:** Same protocol as Week 4. Reduce to 3 sets, drop load to Week 5 levels, cap RPE at 6. Use this week to assess movement quality, address any technique issues, and prepare mentally and physically for the intensity of Phase 3.

---

## Phase 3 — Intensification & Peak (Weeks 9–12)

**Phase Goals:** Maximise strength expression, consolidate hypertrophic gains, and test the client's capacity at near-maximal loads. Rep ranges on primary compounds drop to 3–5. Intensity reaches 82–90% of estimated 1RM. Volume is managed carefully to avoid overreaching. Week 12 is a structured deload and optional testing week.

**Phase 3 Intensity Guidelines:** 82–90% of estimated 1RM on primary compounds. Accessory work remains at 65–72% — do not increase accessory load in this phase; the goal is to preserve hypertrophy stimulus without adding to systemic fatigue.

**Key Changes from Phase 2:**
- Primary compounds move to 5 × 3–5 rep format
- A second heavy compound is retained at 3 × 5–6
- Accessory volume is slightly reduced (drop one set per accessory movement) to manage total fatigue load
- Rest periods on primary compounds extend to 3–4 minutes

---

### Week 9

**Upper A — Push Focus**

- Barbell Bench Press — 5 × 4 @ RPE 8. Rest 3–4 minutes.
- Incline Barbell or Dumbbell Press — 3 × 6 @ RPE 8. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- Cable Chest Fly — 2 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Overhead Tricep Extension — 2 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Lateral Raise — 2 × 15. Rest 60 seconds.
- Dead Bug — 2 × 8 per side. Rest 45 seconds.

**Lower A — Squat Focus**

- Barbell Back Squat — 5 × 4 @ RPE 8. Rest 3–4 minutes.
- Pause Squat — 3 × 4 @ RPE 7–8. Three-second pause at the bottom. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- Leg Press — 2 × 10 @ RPE 7. Rest 90 seconds.
- Walking Lunge — 2 × 10 per leg. Rest 75 seconds.
- Seated Leg Curl — 2 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Standing Calf Raise — 2 × 20. Rest 45 seconds.

**Upper B — Pull Focus**

- Barbell Bent-Over Row — 5 × 4 @ RPE 8. Rest 3–4 minutes.
- Weighted Pull-Up — 3 × 5 @ RPE 8. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- Seated Cable Row — 2 × 10 @ RPE 7. Rest 90 seconds.
- Dumbbell Hammer Curl — 2 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Face Pull — 2 × 15. Rest 60 seconds.
- Pallof Press — 2 × 10 per side. Rest 45 seconds.

**Lower B — Hip Hinge Focus**

- Conventional Deadlift — 5 × 3 @ RPE 8. Rest 3–4 minutes.
- Romanian Deadlift — 3 × 6 @ RPE 8. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 2 × 8 per leg. Rest 90 seconds per leg.
- Hip Thrust — 2 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 90 seconds.
- Leg Extension — 2 × 12 @ RPE 7. Rest 75 seconds.
- Plank — 2 × 45 seconds. Rest 30 seconds.

---

### Weeks 10–11 — Peak Loading

**Week 10:** Increase load on all primary compounds by 2.5–5 kg. Move to 5 × 3 on the bench press and squat. Move to 5 × 2–3 on the deadlift. RPE should reach 8–9 on the final sets. This is the hardest week of the programme. Ensure sleep, nutrition, and stress are managed carefully this week.

**Week 11:** Maintain loads from Week 10 or make small increases (1.25–2.5 kg) only where the client feels strong. This is a consolidation week at near-peak intensity. RPE 8–9. If the client feels fatigued or technique is degrading, hold loads steady — do not push for new maxes yet.

---

### Week 12 — Deload & Optional Strength Testing

**Week 12 Structure:** This is a full deload week with an optional testing component at the end.

**Monday–Thursday:** Reduce all working sets to 3 sets. Drop load to approximately 60–65% of Phase 3 working weights. Perform all four sessions but keep RPE at 5–6 maximum. Focus on movement quality, breathing, and enjoying the training. Sessions should feel almost easy — this is intentional.

**Friday or Saturday (Optional Testing Day):** If the client wishes to test her strength, this is the appropriate time. The deload will have cleared accumulated fatigue and her nervous system will be primed. Suggested testing protocol:

- Barbell Back Squat: Work up to a 3-rep max (3RM) using the following ramp: 50% × 5, 65% × 3, 75% × 2, 82% × 1, 87% × 1, attempt 3RM. Rest 4–5 minutes between heavy attempts.
- Conventional Deadlift: Same ramp protocol, 3RM attempt.
- Barbell Bench Press: Same ramp protocol, 3RM attempt.

Record all results. These numbers become the foundation for the next training block.

---

## Nutrition Guidelines

*Note: These are general evidence-based recommendations. Refer to a registered dietitian for individualised dietary prescription.*

**Energy Intake:** For body composition improvement alongside strength gain, a modest caloric surplus of approximately 100–200 kcal above maintenance is appropriate. This supports muscle protein synthesis and training performance without excessive fat accumulation. If the client's primary goal shifts toward fat loss, a small deficit of 200–300 kcal is acceptable, but note that strength progression will be slower and recovery may be impaired.

**Protein:** Target 1.6–2.2 g per kg of bodyweight per day, distributed across 3–5 meals. Protein is the single most important nutritional variable for this programme. Prioritise whole food sources — chicken, fish, eggs, Greek yoghurt, legumes, tofu — and consider a whey or plant-based protein supplement if hitting targets through food alone is difficult.

**Carbohydrates:** Carbohydrates are the primary fuel for resistance training. Do not restrict them. Prioritise carbohydrate intake around training sessions — a moderate carbohydrate meal 1–2 hours before training and a carbohydrate-protein meal within 1–2 hours after training will support performance and recovery.

**Fats:** Maintain adequate fat intake (0.8–1.2 g per kg bodyweight) for hormonal health, joint lubrication, and fat-soluble vitamin absorption. Prioritise unsaturated sources — olive oil, avocado, nuts, oily fish.

**Hydration:** Aim for 2.5–3 litres of water per day, increasing on training days. Even mild dehydration (1–2% body mass) measurably impairs strength performance.

**Micronutrients of Note:** Iron and calcium deserve attention in female athletes. Ensure adequate dietary iron (red meat, lentils, spinach with vitamin C for absorption) and calcium (dairy, fortified plant milks, leafy greens). The OCP may slightly affect folate and B12 metabolism; a general multivitamin is a reasonable low-cost insurance policy.

---

## Recovery Protocols

**Sleep:** This is non-negotiable. Target 7–9 hours per night. The majority of muscle protein synthesis and hormonal recovery occurs during sleep. If the client is sleeping fewer than 7 hours, address this before adding training volume.

**Active Recovery Days:** On Wednesday and the non-training weekend day, encourage 20–30 minutes of low-intensity activity — walking, light cycling, yoga, or swimming. This promotes blood flow to recovering muscles without adding training stress.

**Soft Tissue Work:** 10 minutes of foam rolling or targeted massage on major working muscle groups post-session is recommended, particularly for the quads, hamstrings, glutes, and thoracic spine. This is not a substitute for sleep or nutrition but supports subjective recovery and mobility.

**Stress Management:** Psychological stress elevates cortisol, which competes with anabolic signalling. If the client is going through a high-stress period (work, personal life), consider reducing training volume temporarily rather than pushing through. A reduced-volume week is far better than an injury or burnout.

**Monitoring Fatigue:** Use a simple daily readiness check — ask the client to rate sleep quality, muscle soreness, motivation, and general energy on a 1–10 scale before each session. If three or more of these scores are below 5, reduce that session's intensity by 20% and do not attempt personal records. Accumulate this data over the 12 weeks; it will be invaluable for programming the next block.

---

## Programme Summary Table

| Phase | Weeks | Primary Rep Range (Compounds) | Intensity (% 1RM) | Target RPE | Volume Focus |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Foundation | 1–3 | 8–12 | 65–72% | 6–7 | High volume, technique |
| 1 — Deload | 4 | 10–12 | 60–65% | ≤6 | Reduced, consolidation |
| 2 — Strength | 5–7 | 4–6 | 75–82% | 7–8 | Moderate-high, load focus |
| 2 — Deload | 8 | 8–10 | 65–70% | ≤6 | Reduced, consolidation |
| 3 — Peak | 9–11 | 3–5 | 82–90% | 8–9 | Moderate, intensity focus |
| 3 — Deload/Test | 12 | 5–6 / Test | 60–65% / Max | ≤6 / Max | Reduced + optional test |

---

## Trainer Notes

**Exercise Substitutions:** If any movement causes pain (not discomfort — pain), substitute immediately. The programme is built around movement patterns, not specific exercises. A trap bar deadlift can replace the conventional deadlift; a Smith machine squat can replace the barbell back squat if rack access is limited; cable rows can replace barbell rows if lower back fatigue is accumulating.

**Load Selection Guidance:** When in doubt, go lighter. A set completed at RPE 6 with perfect technique is worth more than a set ground out at RPE 10 with a rounded back. Especially in Phase 1, the goal is to teach the body to move well under load — the heavy weights will come.
